But the Emperours, and other Christian Soveraigns, [384]
under whose Government these Errours, and the like
encroachments of Ecclesiastiques upon their Office, at
first crept in, to the disturbance of their possessions,
and of the tranquillity of their Subjects, though they
suffered the same for want of foresight of the Sequel,
and of insight into the designs of their Teachers, may
neverthelesse bee esteemed accessaries to their own, and
the Publique dammage: For without their Authority
there could at first no seditious Doctrine have been
publiquely preached. I say they might have hindred
the same in the beginning: But when the people were
